title: Stirling Asymptotic of the Half-Integer Beta Diagonal: B(n+1/2,n+1/2) ~ √(π/n)·4^(-n)

meta.author: Lean Genius
originalContributions: betaDiag_isEquivalent: the large-n asymptotic of the diagonal half-integer Beta value, B(n+1/2,n+1/2) ~ √(π/n)·4^(-n) as n→∞ (Asymptotics.IsEquivalent over atTop). This answers — and CORRECTS — open question oq-01 of the parent entry, which conjectured the asymptotic B(n+1/2,n+1/2) ~ √(π/n). That naive form is false: the central binomial coefficient grows only like 4^n, while the exact value carries 4^(2n) in the denominator, leaving an exponentially decaying residual factor 4^(-n). The correct asymptotic therefore decays geometrically, not merely like n^(-1/2). This matches the classical diagonal Beta asymptotic B(x,x) ~ 2^(1-2x)·√(π/x): at x=n+1/2 the prefactor 2^(1-2x) is exactly 4^(-n).

betaDiag_normalized_tendsto: the explicit normalization, B(n+1/2,n+1/2)·4^n·√(πn)/π → 1. The normalizing factor 4^n·√(πn)/π is exactly the reciprocal of the equivalent √(π/n)·4^(-n); matching it against the central-binomial asymptotic C(2n,n)·√(πn)/4^n → 1 is a pure field identity (the π's cancel and 4^(2n)=4^n·4^n), requiring no square-root manipulation. This is the robust computational heart of the entry.

betaDiag and betaIntegral_eq_betaDiag: a real-valued closed form betaDiag n = π·C(2n,n)/4^(2n) together with a proof that the complex Euler Beta integral Complex.betaIntegral (n+1/2) (n+1/2) equals (betaDiag n : ℂ). This pins the asymptotic to the genuine Beta value rather than to an abstract sequence.

overview.historicalContext: The diagonal of the Euler Beta function, B(x,x) = Γ(x)²/Γ(2x), has a classical large-argument asymptotic B(x,x) ~ 2^(1-2x)·√(π/x), a consequence of Stirling's formula. The half-integer slice x = n+1/2 is special: there the parent entry gave the exact rational-times-π closed form B(n+1/2,n+1/2) = π·C(2n,n)/4^(2n), and the gallery's Stirling line established the central binomial asymptotic C(2n,n) ~ 4^n/√(πn). Combining the two yields the asymptotic of the Beta value with no further analysis. The parent entry, when listing follow-up questions, conjectured the rate as √(π/n) — dropping the exponential prefactor. This entry settles the question and supplies the missing 4^(-n).
overview.problemStatement: Determine the large-n asymptotic of the diagonal half-integer Euler Beta value B(n+1/2,n+1/2). The parent's open question proposed B(n+1/2,n+1/2) ~ √(π/n). Establish the correct asymptotic and prove it as an Asymptotics.IsEquivalent statement over the atTop filter.
overview.proofStrategy: Start from the parent's exact value B(n+1/2,n+1/2) = π·C(2n,n)/4^(2n) and substitute the central binomial asymptotic C(2n,n) ~ 4^n/√(πn): B(n+1/2,n+1/2) ~ π·(4^n/√(πn))/4^(2n) = √(π/n)·4^(-n). Formally, the reciprocal of the candidate equivalent √(π/n)·4^(-n) is the normalizing factor 4^n·√(πn)/π, and B(n+1/2,n+1/2)·4^n·√(πn)/π = C(2n,n)·√(πn)/4^n is a PURE FIELD IDENTITY (the π's cancel, 4^(2n)=4^n·4^n). Hence the normalized ratio tends to 1 by StirlingFormulaOQ03OQ02.centralBinom_asymptotic (Filter.Tendsto.congr), and isEquivalent_iff_tendsto_one upgrades this to B(n+1/2,n+1/2) ~ √(π/n)·4^(-n). The only square-root work is the eventually-true identity √(π/n) = √(πn)/n needed to rewrite the equivalence ratio, handled by Real.mul_self_sqrt and Real.sq_sqrt.
keyInsights: The naive guess B(n+1/2,n+1/2) ~ √(π/n) is FALSE. The central binomial coefficient grows like 4^n, but the exact diagonal value divides by 4^(2n); the mismatch leaves an exponentially small factor 4^(-n). So B(n+1/2,n+1/2) → 0 geometrically, not at the polynomial rate n^(-1/2). Reading off the bare √(π/n) term while forgetting the denominator's 4^(2n) is the trap this entry corrects.

The correct asymptotic √(π/n)·4^(-n) is exactly the classical diagonal Beta law B(x,x) ~ 2^(1-2x)·√(π/x) evaluated at x = n+1/2, where 2^(1-2x) = 2^(-2n) = 4^(-n). The half-integer closed form thus gives a fully elementary, Stirling-powered derivation of the classical prefactor on this slice.

No new analysis is needed: the asymptotic is assembled by pure algebra from two prior gallery results — the parent's exact Beta value and the Stirling line's central binomial asymptotic. The clean matching is engineered by choosing the normalization 4^n·√(πn)/π, the exact reciprocal of the equivalent, so the limit reduces to a field identity rather than a fresh limit computation.

Reciprocity with the integer diagonal extends to rates. The integer diagonal B(n+1,n+1) = 1/((2n+1)·C(2n,n)) decays like 1/(2n·4^n/√(πn)) ~ √(π)/(2·n^(1/2)·4^n) — also carrying a 4^(-n). Both diagonals of the Beta lattice vanish geometrically at rate 4^(-n), modulated by central-binomial polynomial corrections in opposite directions.

The route bypasses Gamma-function Stirling entirely. The textbook derivation of B(x,x) ~ 2^(1-2x)·√(π/x) applies Stirling's asymptotic for Γ directly to Γ(x)²/Γ(2x). This entry instead composes two already-proved gallery results — the exact half-integer closed form (a discrete central-binomial identity) and the discrete central-binomial asymptotic C(2n,n) ~ 4^n/√(πn) — so on the half-integer slice x = n+1/2 the continuous Gamma-Stirling estimate is replaced end-to-end by a purely combinatorial one, giving a second, independent route to the same classical prefactor.

Notes the agreement with the classical B(x,x) ~ 2^(1-2x)·√(π/x) at x=n+1/2 and outlines the pure-field-identity assembly from the parent value and the central binomial asymptotic.

sections.title: The Normalized Limit (Pure Field Identity)
sections.summary: betaDiag_normalized_tendsto proves B(n+1/2,n+1/2)·4^n·√(πn)/π → 1 by transporting StirlingFormulaOQ03OQ02.centralBinom_asymptotic along the pointwise identity C(2n,n)·√(πn)/4^n = betaDiag n·4^n·√(πn)/π. After unfolding and rewriting 4^(2n)=4^n·4^n, field_simp closes the identity outright — no square roots are touched.

sections.title: The IsEquivalent Statement
sections.summary: betaDiag_isEquivalent states B(n+1/2,n+1/2) ~ √(π/n)·4^(-n) using Asymptotics.IsEquivalent. Via isEquivalent_iff_tendsto_one (the equivalent is eventually nonzero for n≥1), the goal reduces to the normalized limit after the eventually-true rewrite √(π/n) = √(πn)/n (proved with Real.mul_self_sqrt) and a final Real.sq_sqrt elimination.

Prove the general diagonal asymptotic B(x,x) ~ 2^(1-2x)·√(π/x) for real x → ∞ (not just the half-integer slice), interpolating this entry's discrete result.

conclusion.summary: The diagonal half-integer Euler Beta value is shown to satisfy B(n+1/2,n+1/2) ~ √(π/n)·4^(-n) as n→∞, an Asymptotics.IsEquivalent statement. The result answers and corrects the parent entry's open question, which conjectured the asymptotic √(π/n): the true rate carries an exponentially decaying factor 4^(-n) because the central binomial grows like 4^n against the 4^(2n) in the denominator. 139 lines, 4 theorems, 1 definition, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.
conclusion.implications: The asymptotic is assembled by pure algebra from two prior gallery results — the parent's exact closed form B(n+1/2,n+1/2)=π·C(2n,n)/4^(2n) and the Stirling line's central binomial asymptotic C(2n,n)~4^n/√(πn) — with a normalization chosen so the limit reduces to a field identity. The corrected rate √(π/n)·4^(-n) coincides with the classical diagonal Beta law B(x,x)~2^(1-2x)·√(π/x) evaluated at x=n+1/2, providing an elementary Stirling-based derivation of its prefactor on the half-integer slice.
